name: Washington
one: Washington mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Washington, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

No request needed

No request is needed: ballots were mailed starting Friday, October 16, 2026 (18 days before the election). If yours has not come, contact your county elections office or print a replacement at VoteWA.gov. Online and mail registrations had to be received by Monday, October 26, 2026 (8 days before Election Day); after that you can still register in person until 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Put your ballot in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, or mail it with a postmark no later than Election Day. A mailed ballot must also arrive before the county certifies the election, which is 21 days after the general election (certification on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, so it must arrive by Monday, November 23). The state recommends mailing it more than a week before Election Day and using a drop box after that. (the law)

Ask for a ballot online, on Washington’s own site

At school away from home, in Washington or in another state? What Washington says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Washington votes by mail in every election. Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically; there is nothing to ask for and no reason to give. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. You do not need to ask for a ballot. Ballots go out at least 18 days before the election. To have it sent to a different address, or to get a replacement, update your mailing address or print a replacement ballot at VoteWA.gov. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Your county elections office or a voting center can give you a replacement ballot. You can also register or update your registration in person until 8 p.m. on Election Day. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • Drop box. Any official ballot drop box, by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The state says drop box ballots by then are guaranteed on time. Find drop boxes at VoteWA.gov. (official page)
  • By mail. By mail, no stamp needed. It must be postmarked no later than Election Day. The state recommends mailing more than a week before Election Day. (the law)
  • In person. At your county elections office or a voting center, by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the declaration on the return envelope. Your county compares that signature with the one on your voter record and will contact you if there is a problem. If you cannot sign, make a mark in front of two witnesses, and they sign in the spaces given. No witness is needed otherwise. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Washington’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Friday, October 16, 2026 to Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Each county opens an accessible voting center starting 18 days before Election Day, until 8 p.m. on Election Day. There you can vote in person, get a replacement ballot, or turn in your mail ballot. Find yours at VoteWA.gov. (official page)

Students

At school in Washington, away from home

Your residential address decides what is on your ballot, and it must be a Washington address you consider home. You may list your home address or your school address. If you list a campus address, include your dorm and room number (a PO box is not a residential address). Your mailing address is just where the ballot is sent, so you can, for example, keep your parents' home as your residential address and have the ballot mailed to a PO box at college. You may vote in only one county; voting in two places is a felony. If two ballots come, vote only one. (official page)

At school in another state, with Washington as home

A Washington student at school in another state, or studying abroad, keeps a Washington address they consider home as their residential address, and the ballot can be mailed anywhere in the world: update your mailing address at VoteWA.gov or with your county. A student from another state may register in Washington if they have a residential address here; voting residency is not the same as residency for in-state tuition. You may vote in only one state, so cancel any registration in another state when you register in Washington. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters (including National Guard, Reserves, and spouses and dependents away because of the service) and overseas voters can register and ask for a ballot through Election Day. You can get your ballot by mail, email or fax. A mailed ballot must have the declaration signed and dated by Election Day and reach your county within 20 days after the November election; a ballot sent by email or fax must arrive by 8 p.m. Pacific Time on Election Day. If your ballot may not arrive in time, you can use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot. (official page)

Washington in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Washington calls a mail ballot an absentee ballot too; every voter gets one.
  • A mailed ballot counts only if postmarked by Election Day. Mail can be slow to get a postmark, so the state recommends mailing more than a week early and using a drop box after that.
  • Sign up for text alerts about your ballot by texting VOTE to 868392 (from the Secretary of State's page).
  • The arrival date for a mailed ballot (November 23) is worked out from the law's rule (received no later than the day before certification, which comes 21 days after the general election); the Secretary of State's pages do not print that date.
  • If you registered to vote without ID, your ballot is not counted until you give your county elections office a qualifying ID (Secretary of State's registration page).
